name: Atacama Desert (Yungay)
description: Hyperarid core of the Atacama; soils so dry and oxidizing that Viking-style life-detection experiments returned Mars-like results.

name: Haughton Crater (Devon Island)
description: 23 km impact crater in a polar desert; home of the NASA Haughton-Mars Project and the FMARS habitat.

name: Death Valley
description: Hot, dry basin with Pleistocene Lake Manly evaporites and the Ubehebe volcanic crater; used to test Mars rover and instrument concepts.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
description: Coldest, driest ice-free terrain on Earth; ground ice, saline ponds and polygons used as a Mars analog for decades.

name: Mauna Kea
description: High basaltic volcano with tephra fields; site of NASA/PISCES lunar ISRU field tests in 2010 and 2012.

name: Mars Desert Research Station
description: Mars Society simulation habitat amid red Jurassic sediments near Hanksville, Utah.

name: Rio Tinto
description: Acidic, iron-rich river system analogous to Meridiani jarosite deposits; NASA MARTE drilling site.

name: Svalbard (Bockfjord)
description: Arctic volcanic complex with carbonate globules like those in Martian meteorite ALH84001; AMASE expedition site.

name: Meteor Crater
description: Young 1.2 km impact crater in Arizona used for Apollo astronaut geology training.

name: Craters of the Moon
description: Basaltic lava fields and tubes in Idaho; Apollo 14 geology training and NASA FINESSE field site.

name: Lanzarote lava tubes
description: La Corona lava tube system; used for ESA PANGAEA and CAVES astronaut training.

name: Iceland lava fields (Askja)
description: Basaltic caldera and tephra plains in the highlands where Apollo astronauts trained in 1965 and 1967.

name: Ladakh (Tso Kar)
description: High-altitude saline lake basin in a cold desert; studied as a Mars analog for evaporites and periglacial landforms.

name: Qaidam Basin (Dalangtan)
description: Hyperarid, high-altitude playa with sulfate and chloride evaporites; studied as a Mars analog.

name: Pavilion Lake
description: Lake with freshwater microbialites; NASA/CSA Pavilion Lake Research Project tested EVA and science operations.

name: Black Point Lava Flow
description: Basaltic flow in northern Arizona used by NASA Desert RATS for rover and spacesuit field tests.

name: Lonar Crater
description: Rare impact crater in Deccan basalt with a saline, alkaline lake; a close analog for craters in Martian basalt.

name: Rann of Kutch
description: Vast seasonal salt marsh; flat evaporite plains comparable to Martian chloride deposits.

name: Spiti Valley
description: Cold Himalayan desert with periglacial landforms and Tethyan sediments.

name: Puga Valley
description: High-altitude hot springs with borax and sulfur deposits in a permafrost setting.

name: Deccan Traps (Mahabaleshwar)
description: Thick flood-basalt sequence, a compositional analog for Martian and lunar mare basalts.

name: Changthang Plateau (Hanle)
description: High cold desert above 4,300 m with saline lakes, low pressure and strong UV.

name: Dasht-e Lut
description: One of the hottest, driest surfaces on Earth, with giant yardangs carved by wind like those on Mars.

name: Danakil Depression (Dallol)
description: Hyperacid, hypersaline hydrothermal field below sea level; tests the limits of habitability.

name: Erta Ale
description: Active basaltic shield volcano with a persistent lava lake in the Afar desert.

name: Namib Desert (Gobabeb)
description: Ancient coastal fog desert with gravel plains and large dune fields.

name: Gobi Desert (Flaming Cliffs)
description: Cold, windy desert with red Cretaceous sediments and wide seasonal temperature swings.

name: Puna de Atacama (Antofalla)
description: High volcanic plateau with salars and basaltic cones, intense UV and low pressure.

name: Salar de Uyuni
description: World's largest salt flat, the remnant of Pleistocene lakes on the Altiplano.

name: Licancabur (Altiplano)
description: 5,900 m volcano with one of the highest lakes on Earth; extreme UV and low pressure.

name: Kerguelen Islands
description: Remote, windswept sub-Antarctic flood-basalt archipelago.

name: Ross Island (Mount Erebus)
description: Polar volcano with fumarolic ice caves, permafrost and an active lava lake.

name: Greenland ice-free margin (Kangerlussuaq)
description: Ice-free terrain at the edge of the Greenland ice sheet with permafrost and glacial outwash.

name: Kamchatka (Tolbachik)
description: Fresh basaltic lava fields and tephra plains with lava tubes from the 2012–13 eruption.

name: Undara lava tubes
description: Among the longest lava tube systems on Earth, formed ~190,000 years ago.

name: Pilbara (Dresser Formation)
description: 3.5-billion-year-old hydrothermal sediments with some of Earth's oldest evidence of life.

name: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre
description: Australia's largest salt lake, usually dry, in the arid interior.

name: Wolfe Creek Crater
description: Well-preserved 880 m meteorite crater in the Great Sandy Desert.

name: Gosses Bluff
description: Eroded central uplift of a 142-million-year-old impact structure.

name: Popigai Crater
description: 100 km impact structure in Siberian permafrost, rich in impact diamonds.

name: Lake El'gygytgyn
description: 3.6-million-year-old Arctic impact crater lake with a continuous sediment record.

name: Pingualuit Crater
description: Young 3.4 km impact crater in the Nunavik tundra.

name: Manicouagan Crater
description: Large impact structure with impact melt over anorthositic target rocks.

name: Mistastin Lake Crater
description: One of very few terrestrial impact craters in anorthosite, the dominant lunar highland rock.

name: Stillwater Complex
description: Layered intrusion with anorthosite used as feedstock for NASA lunar highland regolith simulants.

name: Merriam Crater cinders
description: Basaltic cinder deposit near Flagstaff, source of the JSC-1 lunar regolith simulant.

name: Lava Beds
description: More than 700 lava tube caves, several with perennial ice.

name: El Malpais
description: Young basalt flows with lava tubes and ice caves in New Mexico.

name: Jeju lava tubes (Manjanggul)
description: Large, accessible basaltic lava tube system on a volcanic island.

name: Harrat Khaybar
description: Arid basaltic lava field with cinder cones and lava tubes such as Umm Jirsan.

name: Rub' al Khali
description: The largest continuous sand desert on Earth.

name: Tibesti (Emi Koussi)
description: Large shield volcano with a summit caldera in the central Sahara.

name: Kamil Crater
description: Pristine 45 m iron-meteorite crater in the hyperarid Western Desert.

name: Lop Nur
description: Dried salt lake with yardangs in the Tarim Basin; one of the driest places in Asia.

name: Ngari (western Tibet)
description: High, cold, dry plateau with saline lakes and periglacial terrain.

name: Axel Heiberg Island
description: Perennial cold saline springs flowing through thick permafrost.

name: Allan Hills
description: Blue-ice field where Martian meteorite ALH84001 was found.

name: Ojos del Salado
description: The highest volcano on Earth; dry, cold, low-pressure summit region with permafrost.

name: Kilimanjaro summit
description: Equatorial volcanic summit above 5,800 m with low pressure and intense UV.

name: Lac Assal
description: Hypersaline lake in basaltic rift terrain, 155 m below sea level.

name: Wadi Rum
description: Red sandstone desert valleys often used to depict Mars on film.

name: Ka'u Desert (Kilauea)
description: Barren basalt and tephra fields downwind of Kilauea's acid gas plume.

name: Fernandina Island
description: Young, active basaltic shield volcano in the Galápagos.

name: Salar de Atacama
description: Large salt flat on the edge of the hyperarid Atacama.

name: Batagaika Crater
description: Huge thaw slump exposing hundreds of thousands of years of Siberian ground ice.

name: Pinacate volcanic field
description: Basaltic field with large maar craters in the Sonoran Desert.

name: Cuatro Ciénegas
description: Desert basin with gypsum dunes and living stromatolites.

name: White Sands
description: The largest gypsum dune field on Earth, like Mars' north-polar gypsum dunes.

name: Monturaqui Crater
description: Small impact crater in the hyperarid, high Atacama.

name: Wabar Craters
description: Iron-meteorite craters in the sand sea of the Rub' al Khali.

name: Hoggar (Atakor)
description: Volcanic highland of basalt plateaus and phonolite spires in the central Sahara.
